content: The C2 JU requests or reports track filters in separate J7.6 messages from reference point and EW product filters.
rationale: The claim is directly supported by Evidence [milstd6016b_sec4:P135#C454] line c, which explicitly states that track filters shall be requested/reported in separate J7.6 messages from reference point and EW product filters.

content: When a transmit filter is activated, the C2 JU ceases reporting any track for which it has R2 and which meets the filter criteria.
rationale: The claim is a direct paraphrase of Evidence [milstd6016b_sec4:P133#C448] item h, which explicitly states that when a transmit filter is activated, the unit shall cease reporting tracks meeting the criteria for which it has R2.

content: The C2 JU applies filters to tracks initiated prior to filter activation as well as to tracks initiated while the filter is active.
rationale: The claim is directly supported by Evidence [milstd6016b_sec4:P133#C448] item h, which explicitly states that filters apply to tracks initiated prior to filter activation as well as to tracks initiated while the filter is active.

content: The C2 JU ensures tracks are eligible for transmission on the interface only if they are not inhibited from transmission by any of the transmission filters currently set.
rationale: The evidence states the general rule for track eligibility but does not specify that the 'C2 JU' is the actor ensuring this condition, leaving the agent attribution unsupported.

content: The C2 JU does not request or report the use of receive filters via Link 16.
rationale: The evidence explicitly states that the use of receive filters is neither requested nor reported via Link 16, which directly supports the claim.

content: The C2 JU may filter C2 IUs with the Simulation Indicator field set in their J2 PPLI message; active nonsimulated C2 IUs cannot be filtered.
rationale: The evidence explicitly states that active nonsimulated C2 IUs cannot be filtered and implies that C2 IUs with the Simulation Indicator set may be filtered, fully supporting the claim.

content: The C2 JU does not filter any track or nonC2 IU with an EMG IND or FT IND set to the value of 1.
rationale: The evidence explicitly states that any track or nonC2 IU with EMG IND or FT IND set to 1 shall not be filtered, which directly supports the claim.

content: At main flow step 0, if the transmit filter is a special processing filter, a JU filters data based on the setting of the Special Processing Indicator field.
rationale: The evidence defines what a special processing filter is but does not mention 'main flow step 0' or establish the conditional branching logic required for an alternative flow claim.

content: At main flow step 0, if the transmit filter is a simulation filter, a JU filters data and IUs based on the setting of the Simulation Indicator field.
rationale: The evidence confirms that a simulation filter allows filtering based on the Simulation Indicator field, but it does not support the claim's specific reference to 'main flow step 0' or the conditional structure of an alternative flow step.

content: At main flow step 0, if the transmit filter is an environment/category filter, a JU filters tracks and nonC2 IUs from the space, air, surface (maritime), subsurface (maritime), and land (ground) environment/categories, as well as reference points and electronic warfare product information.
rationale: The claim's description of how an environment/category filter functions is directly supported by the text in section 4.7.7.2 of the evidence.

content: At main flow step 0, if the transmit filter is an ID filter, a JU filters tracks and nonC2 IUs based on their IDs; Exercise Indicator settings have no influence on ID filters, and Identity and Identity Amplifying Descriptor are filtered in the same manner.
rationale: The claim is fully supported by Evidence [milstd6016b_sec4:P127#C424], which explicitly states that an ID filter filters tracks/nonC2 IUs based on IDs, Exercise Indicator settings have no influence, and Identity/Identity Amplifying Descriptor are filtered in the same manner.

content: At main flow step 0, if the transmit filter is a geographic filter, a JU filters tracks and nonC2 IUs based on their geographic location; maximum and minimum altitude values may also be defined for each filter to describe volumes; filters can be fixed geographically, slaved to the filtering JU or some other moving reference point, or move independently.
rationale: The claim is fully supported by the evidence text which defines geographic filters, their altitude parameters, and movement types.

content: At main flow step 0, if the filter is a message label/sublabel filter, the J7.6 message shall not be used to request implementation/deletion or status of message label/sublabel filters, and this type of filter will not be reported in the J7.6 Filter Description Report; if implemented, the message label/sublabel filter shall only be used for the purposes described and shall not be used as a data filter.
rationale: The evidence supports the restrictions on message label/sublabel filters but does not mention 'main flow step 0' or establish this as a conditional branch within a use-case interaction flow.

content: At main flow step 0, filters requested or reported in J7.6 do not apply to any messages other than the J2, J3, and J12 (on Needline PG) series messages listed, except a simulation filter applies to C2 IUs.
rationale: The claim is directly supported by Evidence [milstd6016b_sec4:P135#C454] line b, which states that filters in J7.6 messages do not apply to messages other than the listed J2, J3, and J12 series, with the specific exception for simulation filters on C2 IUs.

content: At main flow step 5, an exception to requesting/reporting track filters in separate J7.6 messages from reference point and EW product filters applies if in a track filter message the Unknown E/C Filter Indicator is set to value 1.
rationale: The evidence supports the exception rule regarding the Unknown E/C Filter Indicator but does not mention 'main flow step 5' or link this rule to a specific step in a use-case main flow.

content: At main flow step 6, if a track or nonC2 IU has an EMG IND or FT IND set to the value of 1, it shall not be filtered.

content: At main flow step 9, if a system filters tracks/IUs on receipt, it must establish a transmit filter which duplicates the receive filter; when a receive filter is geographically defined, the transmit filter must, where possible, be defined to permit the area filtered for transmission to be slightly larger than the area filtered for reception so that tracks entering or leaving the filtered area may be displayed to the operator to prevent dual designations.
rationale: The claim is fully supported by the evidence text which mandates the transmit filter duplication and geographic expansion rules.

content: At main flow step 10, if a C2 IU is active nonsimulated, it cannot be filtered.
rationale: The evidence explicitly states that active nonsimulated C2 IUs cannot be filtered, directly supporting the claim's condition and outcome.

content: If the filter is a receive filter, the use of receive filters is neither requested nor reported via Link 16; exit by not requesting or reporting receive filters via Link 16.
rationale: The evidence explicitly states that the use of receive filters is neither requested nor reported via Link 16, which directly supports the claim's condition and resulting behavior.

content: If forwarding unit filters are for forwarding data from any other link to Link 16, they are neither requested nor reported via Link 16; exit by not requesting or reporting such forwarding unit filters via Link 16.
rationale: The evidence explicitly states that filters for forwarding data from any other link to Link 16 are neither requested nor reported via Link 16, directly supporting the claim's condition and outcome.

content: If filters requested or reported in the J7.6 messages are for messages other than the J2, J3, and J12 (on Needline PG) series messages listed, they do not apply, except a simulation filter applies to C2 IUs; exit by not applying those filters to other messages.
rationale: The claim is directly supported by Evidence [milstd6016b_sec4:P135#C454] line b, which states that filters in J7.6 messages do not apply to messages other than the specified J2, J3, and J12 series, with the specific exception for simulation filters on C2 IUs.

content: If any track or nonC2 IU has an EMG IND or FT IND set to the value of 1, it shall not be filtered; exit by not filtering that track or nonC2 IU.
rationale: The claim is directly supported by Evidence [milstd6016b_sec4:P132#C446] item d, which states that tracks or nonC2 IUs with EMG IND or FT IND set to 1 shall not be filtered.

content: If a C2 IU is active nonsimulated, it cannot be filtered; exit by not filtering active nonsimulated C2 IUs. C2 IUs with the Simulation Indicator field set in their J2 PPLI message may be filtered.
rationale: The claim is directly supported by Evidence [milstd6016b_sec4:P133#C448] which states that active nonsimulated C2 IUs cannot be filtered and those with the Simulation Indicator set may be filtered.

content: If the storage files of a JU are filled and all applicable filters have been used, acceptance of the new data shall not be required, regardless of its ID or priority; this procedure applies to both real-time and nonrealtime data. Exit by not requiring acceptance of the new data.

content: If a C2 JU is deactivating a receive filter, after initially achieving Active status or after returning to Active status from Inactive status or TDS Failure, it shall not transmit air, surface, or land tracks until sufficient reporting responsibility checks, correlation, and data registration are performed; the minimum wait before reporting air and surface tracks is 12 seconds and for land tracks is 48 seconds. Exit by delaying track transmission until the minimum wait is satisfied.
rationale: The claim is fully supported by the evidence, which explicitly states that C2 JUs deactivating a receive filter must not transmit tracks until checks are performed and specifies the 12-second and 48-second minimum wait times.

content: The use of interface filters has been coordinated with all IUs to minimize track management problems.

content: All filters are identified by filter number for coordination with other JUs.

content: Tracks are eligible for transmission on the interface only if they are not inhibited from transmission by any of the transmission filters currently set.

content: Filters apply to tracks initiated prior to filter activation as well as to tracks initiated while the filter is active.

rationale: The claim is a direct paraphrase of Evidence [milstd6016b_sec4:P133#C448] item h, which explicitly states that upon filter activation, the unit shall cease reporting tracks meeting the criteria.

content: Active nonsimulated C2 IUs are not filtered; C2 IUs with the Simulation Indicator field set in their J2 PPLI message may be filtered.

content: Voice coordination capability must be available in addition to the filter message mechanism to ensure filter management on the interface.

content: A JU requests that a filter be implemented by another JU, or reports a filter which the JU has inserted into its TDS, or responds to a J7.1 (ACT = 0) message.

content: The C2 JU determines the filter types and parameters for each type, specifying whether to filter inside or outside the defined area.

content: The C2 JU sends a J7.6 (ACT = 0) message to request that a filter be implemented by another JU, with the Filter Number field set to value 0.

content: The C2 JU performs voice coordination in addition to sending the filter message to ensure filter management on the interface.

content: If specific filters have been prearranged, the C2 JU may implement the request by specifying the filter number with all Filter Indicator fields of the J7.6 (ACT = 0) set to value 0.

content: The C2 JU may send a J7.6 (ACT = 2) Delete Filter Request/Report message to manage existing filters.

content: Transmit filters, including data forwarding filters, have been coordinated between JUs as specified by the Filter Unit Type field indicating whether the filter applies to individual JU transmissions or forwarding unit transmissions of forwarded data.

content: If a J7.6 (ACT = 1) Filter Description Report was sent, the filter number has been set to a value between 1 and 14, and if responding to a J7.1 (ACT = 0) message, the message(s) have been addressed to the JU requesting the filter information.
rationale: The evidence explicitly states that for a J7.6 (ACT = 1) message, the filter number shall be set to a value between 1 and 14, and when responding to a J7.1 (ACT = 0), the message(s) shall be addressed to the requesting JU.

content: Any new filter report on a previously received filter number from a JU has superseded prior filter data for that number.

content: In the case of a line or area filter requiring multiple messages with the same filter number, all messages have been treated as a single filter report.

content: Coordinate filter activation/deletion via J7.6 messages to control track transmission
rationale: The evidence explicitly states that management and reporting of transmit filters (activation/deletion) are accomplished using J7.6 messages, and that these filters control track transmission eligibility.

content: The C2 JU has established communication channels (voice or other media) with all IUs for coordination of filtering requests.

content: The C2 JU is operating on Needline PGs and is subject to data filtering rules as defined in sub-paragraphs a. through i.

content: No active transmit filters are currently inhibiting transmission of tracks that meet filter criteria, unless intentionally activated per prior coordination.

content: The J7.6 message mechanism is available for requesting or reporting insertion/deletion of transmit filters.

content: When a transmit filter is activated by a unit, the unit shall cease reporting any track for which it has R² and which meets the filter criteria, and shall comply with rules for terminating transmission of applicable track data.

content: Filters apply to tracks initiated prior to filter activation as well as those initiated while the filter is active.

content: Upon activation of a transmit filter, the unit ceases reporting any track for which it has R² that meets the filter criteria and complies with rules for terminating transmission of applicable track data.

content: The J7.2 Correlation message shall not be inhibited by any filter.

content: The C2 JU has an automatic decorrelation capability for real-time air or surface tracks it initiates, or it is performing manual decorrelation, which C2 JUs may also do.

content: The tracks meet the applicable decorrelation criteria.

content: After decorrelation, the C2 JU initiates a surveillance track report with locally held data using a new track number.

content: 1. If TN A is controlled by own unit; i.e., is the subject of own unit reported J10.5 Controlling Unit Report message, do not automatically decorrelate; exit the automatic decorrelation path. If manually decorrelated, alert the operator as a cue to report termination of control TN A if appropriate. Report commencement of control of TN B using the J10.5 message only if initiated by operator action.

content: If TN A had been correlated with an Index Number by own unit, whether the Index Number should remain with TN A or B has been assessed, and J12.5 messages have been transmitted as appropriate.

A J7.0 (ACT = 0) Drop Track message is received from the FJU for a PU, RU, or other IU, or d. The Geodetic Position Quality in the J2 PPLI message is set to value 0.
rationale: The claim is a verbatim extraction of section 4.4.2.2.2 from the source page, which explicitly lists the four conditions (a-d) under which a C² JU assumes R² of an IU.

content: When a C² JU recognizes that two tracks which are being reported to the interface are eligible for correlation, that JU shall initiate action, either automatically or manually, to resolve the dual designation.
rationale: The claim is a verbatim extraction of the first sentence of paragraph 4.7.3.b on page P113, which explicitly states that when a C² JU recognizes eligible tracks, it shall initiate action to resolve the dual designation.

content: The recognizing JU shall transmit the J7.2 Correlation message requesting all other C² IUs to perform a correlation of the two tracks.
rationale: The claim is a direct paraphrase of the sentence in paragraph 4.7.3.b stating that the recognizing JU shall transmit the J7.2 Correlation message requesting all other C² IUs to perform a correlation of the two tracks.

content: The message identifies the TN to be retained and the TN to be dropped.
rationale: The claim is a direct verbatim extraction from paragraph b of the source text, which explicitly states that the J7.2 Correlation message identifies the TN to be retained and the TN to be dropped.

content: The receiving IUs shall accept the requested correlation unless certain prespecified conditions exist which require or allow the receiving IU to reject the requested correlation or respond with a reverse correlation request.
rationale: The claim is a verbatim extraction from paragraph 4.7.3.b of the source text, which explicitly states that receiving IUs shall accept the requested correlation unless specific prespecified conditions exist allowing rejection or reverse correlation.

content: If a correlation is found with a track for which the C² JU has R², the J7.2 Correlation message shall be transmitted with the Response Value (RV) field set to value 1 (Reverse Correlation Not Acceptable), and with the Source TN in the Header word of the J2 PPLI message as the Retained TN and the surveillance TN as the Dropped TN.
rationale: The claim is a verbatim extraction of the procedural steps defined in paragraph 4.4.2.2.1.b regarding the system's response to a specific correlation condition.

content: The C² JU shall cease reporting the track and transmit a J7.0 (ACT = 0) Drop Track message on the surveillance TN.
rationale: The claim is a verbatim extraction of the final sentence in paragraph 4.4.2.2.1.b, which prescribes the specific actions (ceasing reporting and transmitting J7.0) the C² JU must take upon finding a correlation with a track for which it has R².

content: If the receiving IU has any constraint which would prohibit accepting a reverse correlation, it shall set the Response Value (RV) field to value 0 in its J7.2 message to indicate that a reverse correlation would be acceptable.
rationale: The evidence explicitly states that when the RV field is set to value 0 it indicates a reverse correlation would be acceptable, whereas value 1 indicates it would be rejected; the claim incorrectly asserts that having a constraint prohibiting acceptance corresponds to setting RV to 0.

content: If the receiving IU indicates in its J7.2 message that a reverse correlation request should be rejected (RV = 2), the originating JU shall reject the original correlation request.
rationale: The evidence explicitly states that RV=2 is used to report the rejection of a correlation request, whereas the claim incorrectly asserts that RV=2 indicates a reverse correlation request should be rejected (which the text assigns to RV=1).

content: When the RV field is set to value 3 in the J7.2 message, it indicates the correlation was manually initiated and shall be accepted unless certain conditions apply which require rejection.
rationale: The claim is a direct paraphrase of the sentence in paragraph 4.7.3.b stating that RV field value 3 indicates manual initiation and acceptance unless specific rejection conditions apply.

content: If a correlation is found with a track for which another C² JU has R² and the TNs are different, the J7.2 (RV = 1) Correlation message shall be transmitted, with the Source TN in the Header word of the J2 PPLI message as the Retained TN and the surveillance TN as the Dropped TN.
rationale: The claim is a verbatim extraction of paragraph 4.4.2.2.1.c on page P7, which explicitly defines the system behavior when a correlation is found with a track owned by another C² JU with different TNs.

content: If a correlation is found with a track for which another C² JU has R² and the TNs are the same, the JU receiving the J2 shall accept the PPLI information into its surveillance database and shall disregard the J3 surveillance data on the specified track except when Geodetic Position Quality in the PPLI message is set to value 0, in which case the surveillance track is accepted and the PPLI message shall be discarded.
rationale: The claim is a verbatim extraction of paragraph 4.4.2.2.1.d from the source page, fully supported by the text describing the specific correlation scenario where TNs are the same.

content: If the receiving IU has any constraint which would prohibit accepting a reverse correlation, it shall set the Response Value (RV) field to value 0 in its J7.2 message to indicate that a reverse correlation would be acceptable.
rationale: The evidence explicitly states that setting the RV field to value 0 indicates a reverse correlation would be acceptable, whereas the claim asserts that value 0 is used when a constraint prohibits accepting a reverse correlation, which directly contradicts the source text defining value 1 as the indicator for rejection.

content: If the receiving IU indicates in its J7.2 message that a reverse correlation request should be rejected (RV = 2), the originating JU shall reject the original correlation request.
rationale: The evidence explicitly states that RV=2 is used to report the rejection of a correlation request, whereas the claim incorrectly asserts that RV=2 indicates a reverse correlation request should be rejected (which the text assigns to RV=1).

content: When the RV field is set to value 3 in the J7.2 message, it indicates the correlation was manually initiated and shall be accepted unless certain conditions apply which require rejection.
rationale: The claim is a direct paraphrase of the sentence in paragraph 4.7.3.b stating that RV value 3 indicates manual initiation and acceptance unless specific rejection conditions apply.

content: If a correlation is found with a track for which another C² JU has R² and the TNs are different, the J7.2 (RV = 1) Correlation message shall be transmitted, with the Source TN in the Header word of the J2 PPLI message as the Retained TN and the surveillance TN as the Dropped TN.
rationale: The claim is a verbatim extraction of paragraph 4.4.2.2.1.c on page P7, which explicitly defines the system response when correlation is found with a track owned by another C² JU with different TNs.

content: If a correlation is found with a track for which another C² JU has R² and the TNs are the same, the JU receiving the J2 shall accept the PPLI information into its surveillance database and shall disregard the J3 surveillance data on the specified track except when Geodetic Position Quality in the PPLI message is set to value 0, in which case the surveillance track is accepted and the PPLI message shall be discarded.
rationale: The claim is a verbatim reproduction of paragraph 4.4.2.2.1.d on page P7, which explicitly defines the system behavior when correlation is found with a track owned by another C² JU having the same TN.

content: The C² JU has accepted and reported the change in force tell status in its J2 message.
rationale: The evidence states that the JU whose status is being changed shall accept and report the change, but does not specify that this actor must be a C² JU; additionally, the claim describes an intermediate response action rather than a final system state.

content: Other receiving JUs have set or cleared the alert indicator in their databases upon receipt of the J7.0 (ACT = 4) message.
rationale: The source text explicitly states that 'The other JUs shall set/clear the alert indicator in their databases upon receipt of the J7.0 (ACT = 4) message,' which directly supports the claim's description of the resulting state.

content: Optionally, other JUs may have cleared the alert indicator upon reception of a J2 message with FT IND set to value 0.
rationale: The claim is directly supported by the final sentence of the last paragraph on page P102, which states: 'Optionally, other JUs may clear the alert indicator upon reception of a J2 message with FT IND set to value 0.'

content: Enable the C2 JU to initiate and clear surveillance track alerts (force tell and emergency) by setting or clearing appropriate alert indicators in J-series messages.
rationale: The evidence explicitly states that a C2 JU shall have the capability to initiate/terminate a force tell alert by setting/clearing the FT IND in a J7.0 message (P102), and P10/P104/P105 confirm that track alerts consist of force tell and emergency indicators set in J-series messages.

content: The C2 JU must have the capability to initiate/terminate a force tell alert on another JU by setting/clearing the FT IND in a J7.0 (ACT = 4) message.
rationale: The claim is directly supported by the text on page 102 which states 'A C2 JU shall have the capability to initiate/terminate a force tell alert on another JU by setting/clearing the FT IND in a J7.0 (ACT = 4) message.'

content: For tracks, the initiating JU must possess R² capability to set EMG IND or FT IND in J3.2, J3.3, J3.4, or J3.5 messages; otherwise, it must use J7.0 (ACT = 3 or 4).
rationale: The claim accurately synthesizes the rules from P104 (JU with R² sets indicators in J3.x) and P105 (JU without R² uses J7.0), which are directly supported by the cited text.

content: For land (ground) points or subsurface contacts, the initiating JU must possess R² capability to set EMG IND or FT IND in J3.5 (PTI = 0) or J5.4 messages; otherwise, it must use J7.0 (ACT = 3 or 4).
rationale: The evidence explicitly states that a JU with R² initiates alerts via J3.5/J5.4 messages, while a JU without R² must use J7.0 (ACT = 3 or 4), fully supporting the claim's conditional requirement.

content: For Electronic Warfare Product Information, the initiating JU must possess R² capability to set EMG IND or FT IND in the J3.7 message; otherwise, it must use J7.0 (ACT = 3 or 4).
rationale: The evidence explicitly states that a JU with R² initiates alerts via J3.7 and a JU without R² uses J7.0 (ACT = 3 or 4), fully supporting the claim's conditional logic.

content: The C2 JU operator initiates an action to set or clear the emergency (EMG IND) or force tell (FT IND) alert indicators for a surveillance track.
rationale: The evidence specifies that a JU with R² initiates alerts on tracks by setting indicators in J3 messages and a JU without R² does so via J7.0 messages, but it does not explicitly state that a 'C2 JU operator' performs this initiation or that the action is specifically for a 'surveillance track'.

content: A JU with R² capability initiates an emergency or force tell alert on a surveillance track by setting the appropriate EMG IND or FT IND in the J3.2 Air Track, J3.3 Surface Track, J3.4 Subsurface Track, or J3.5 Land Point/Track message.
rationale: The claim is directly supported by the text under section 4.7.1.4.5 'ALERT INDICATORS FOR TRACKS', which states that a JU with R² shall initiate an emergency or force tell alert on tracks by setting the appropriate EMG IND or FT IND in the specified J3.2 through J3.5 messages.

content: All receiving JUs accept the alert indicator set by the initiating JU in their databases upon receipt of the J3.X track message.
rationale: The evidence explicitly states that 'All receiving JUs shall accept the alert in their databases' when a JU initiates an alert by setting indicators in J3.X track messages.

content: A JU with R² capability terminates an emergency or force tell alert by transmitting a J7.0 (ACT = 3 or 4) message to terminate the alert.
rationale: The claim is directly supported by the text in section 4.7.1.4.5 which states that 'The JU with R² shall terminate an emergency or force tell alert by transmitting a J7.0 (ACT = 3 or 4) message terminating the alert'.

content: After sending the J7.0 termination message, the initiating JU sets the appropriate EMG IND or FT IND field to 0 in subsequent J3.2, J3.3, J3.4, or J3.5 messages for that track.
rationale: The evidence explicitly states that the JU with R² shall terminate an alert by transmitting a J7.0 message and setting the appropriate EMG IND or FT IND field to 0 in subsequent J3.2, J3.3, J3.4, or J3.5 messages.

content: All receiving JUs terminate the alert in their databases upon receipt of the J7.0 (ACT = 3 or 4) message.
rationale: The claim is directly supported by the text in section 4.7.1.4.5 which states: 'All receiving JUs shall terminate the alert in their databases upon receipt of the J7.0 (ACT = 3 or 4) message.'

content: Optionally, alerts may be cleared by reception of a J3.X message with the EMG IND and/or FT IND set to value 0.
rationale: The claim is a verbatim extraction from the final sentence of section 4.7.1.4.5 on page P104, which explicitly states that alerts may optionally be cleared by reception of a J3.X message with specific indicator values.

content: A JU without R² capability initiates or terminates an emergency or force tell alert by setting or clearing the appropriate EMG IND or FT IND in a J7.0 (ACT = 3 or 4) message.
rationale: The claim is directly supported by the text on page P105 which states: 'A JU without R² shall initiate/terminate an emergency or force tell alert by setting/clearing the appropriate EMG IND or FT IND in a J7.0 (ACT = 3 or 4) message.'

content: Upon receipt of a J7.0 (ACT = 3 or 4) message from a JU without R², the JU with R² sets or clears the appropriate EMG IND or FT IND in the J3.2, J3.3, J3.4, or J3.5 message.
rationale: The claim is directly supported by the second paragraph on page P105, which states that upon receipt of a J7.0 (ACT = 3 or 4) message from a JU without R², the JU with R² shall set/clear the appropriate EMG IND or FT IND in the J3.2, J3.3, J3.4, or J3.5 message.

content: Optionally, alerts on tracks may be cleared by reception of a J3.X message (J3.2, J3.3, J3.4, or J3.5) with the EMG IND and/or FT IND set to value 0, instead of requiring a J7.0 (ACT = 3 or 4) termination message.
rationale: The claim is directly supported by the final sentence of section 4.7.1.4.5 on page 104, which states that alerts may optionally be cleared by reception of a J3.X message with indicators set to 0.

content: A JU without R² capability initiates or terminates an emergency or force tell alert on tracks by setting/clearing the appropriate EMG IND or FT IND in a J7.0 (ACT = 3 or 4) message; upon receipt, the JU with R² sets/clears the indicator in subsequent J3.2, J3.3, J3.4, or J3.5 messages.
rationale: The claim is fully supported by the second paragraph of page P105, which explicitly describes the procedure for a JU without R² to initiate/terminate alerts via J7.0 and the corresponding response by the JU with R² in J3.X messages.

content: For Electronic Warfare Product Information, optionally, alerts may be cleared by reception of a J3.7 message with the EMG IND and/or FT IND set to value 0, as an alternative to J7.0 termination.
rationale: The source text explicitly states that alerts may optionally be cleared by reception of a J3.7 message with EMG/FT IND set to 0, which supports the claim's description of an alternative clearing mechanism.

content: For land (ground) points or subsurface contacts, optionally, alerts may be cleared by reception of a J3.5 or J5.4 message with the EMG IND and/or FT IND set to 0, instead of using J7.0 (ACT = 3 or 4).
rationale: The claim is directly supported by the text in section 4.7.1.4.6 which states: 'Optionally, alerts may be cleared by reception of a J3.5 or J5.4 message with the EMG IND and/or FT IND set to 0.'

content: When terminating a force tell alert on a track, the JU shall also terminate the force tell alert on any reference point or area that is slaved to the track.
rationale: The claim is directly supported by the text in the second paragraph of page 104, which states: 'A JU terminating a force tell alert on a track shall also terminate the force tell alert on any reference point or area that is slaved to the track.'

content: A JU initiating a force tell alert on a slaved reference point or area shall also initiate an alert on the Related TN if it does not already have the FT IND set; when terminating the alert for the reference point or area, the JU shall also terminate the alert for the Related TN unless it had the FT IND set prior to initiation.
rationale: The claim is a direct paraphrase of the second paragraph on page 104, which explicitly defines the conditional initiation and termination logic for alerts on Related TNs when operating on slaved reference points or areas.

content: For reference points, lines, and areas, optionally, alerts may be cleared by reception of a J3.0 message with the FT IND set to value 0, as an alternative to J7.0 (ACT = 4) termination.
rationale: The source text explicitly states in two separate paragraphs that 'Optionally, alerts may be cleared by reception of a J3.0 message with FT IND set to value 0,' directly supporting the claim's description of an optional clearing mechanism.

content: If a system with limited track capacity (e.g., F-15) is at risk of being saturated by force tell and emergency alerts, it must manage its database to ensure it shall not be saturated.
rationale: The claim is directly supported by the text in section 4.4.2.5 which states that a system with limited track capacity (e.g., F-15) should manage its database to insure that it shall not be saturated by force tell and emergency alerts.

content: A JU shall not initiate or terminate an emergency alert on another Active JU; this action is prohibited.
rationale: The claim is directly supported by the sentence on page 102 stating 'A JU shall not initiate or terminate an emergency alert on another Active JU.'

content: All receiving JUs have accepted the alert indicator (EMG IND or FT IND) set by the initiating JU in their databases upon receipt of the J3.X track message (J3.2, J3.3, J3.4, or J3.5).
rationale: The evidence states that receiving JUs accept alerts upon receipt of the J3.X message containing the indicator, but it does not support the claim's specific condition that this acceptance occurs 'upon receipt of the J3.X track message... set by the initiating JU', as the text describes acceptance of the indicator's presence in the message rather than a causal link to the initiator's setting action at that moment.

content: All receiving JUs have terminated the alert in their databases upon receipt of the J7.0 (ACT = 3 or 4) termination message.
rationale: The evidence on pages P105 and P106 explicitly states that 'All receiving JUs shall terminate the alert in their databases upon receipt of the J7.0 (ACT = 3 or 4) message' for multiple track types.

content: The initiating JU has set the appropriate EMG IND or FT IND field to 0 in subsequent J3.2, J3.3, J3.4, or J3.5 messages for that track after sending the J7.0 termination message.
rationale: Page 105 explicitly states that the JU with R² shall terminate an alert by transmitting a J7.0 message and 'setting the EMG IND or FT IND in subsequent J3.2, J3.3, J3.4, or J3.5 messages to value 0', which directly supports the claim's description of the resulting state.

content: For Electronic Warfare Product Information, all receiving JUs have accepted the alert in their databases upon receipt of the J3.7 message with EMG IND or FT IND set.
rationale: The evidence on P106 states that receiving JUs accept the alert upon receipt of the J3.7 message containing the indicator, whereas the claim incorrectly asserts acceptance occurs upon receipt of a J3.7 message with the indicator set (which describes the optional clearing mechanism).

content: For land (ground) points or subsurface contacts, all receiving JUs have accepted the alert upon receipt of the J3.5 (PTI = 0) or J5.4 message with EMG IND or FT IND set.
rationale: Page 105 explicitly states that for land (ground) points or subsurface contacts, 'All receiving JUs shall accept the alert' when a JU with R² initiates it by setting the EMG IND or FT IND in the J3.5 (PTI = 0) or J5.4 message.

content: To report ballistic missile surveillance tracks/points on the interface so that C2 JU provides complete, accurate, timely, correlated information in accordance with R2 reporting rules.
rationale: The claim accurately synthesizes the reporting criteria (complete, accurate, timely, correlated) and R2 rules from the evidence into a coherent objective for the C2 JU.

content: The C2 JU has R2 for the ballistic missile track to be reported.
rationale: The evidence explicitly states that a JU transmits a track report for a ballistic missile only when it has R2 for that track, directly supporting the claim that having R2 is a necessary condition.

content: For an initial surveillance report on a ballistic missile, the predicted time to impact is not less than 16 seconds.
rationale: The evidence explicitly states that an initial surveillance report shall not be transmitted if the predicted time to impact is less than 16 seconds, which logically entails that for any such report that is transmitted, the time must be at least 16 seconds.

content: For an initial Ballistic Missile surveillance report on a descending ballistic missile, the altitude of the descending ballistic missile is not less than 8 data miles.
rationale: The evidence explicitly states that an initial report shall not be transmitted if the altitude is less than 8 data miles, which logically entails that for a report to be transmitted, the altitude must be not less than 8 data miles.

content: When a related TN for an Impact Point is used, the C2 JU has R2 for the related missile track.
rationale: The evidence explicitly states that a related TN for an Impact Point is used only by the C2 JU with R2 for the related missile track, directly supporting the claim's condition and state.

content: The local ballistic missile track to be reported is uncorrelated with ballistic missile tracks reported on the Surveillance NPG.
rationale: The evidence states that the system must report uncorrelated tracks, but it does not explicitly state that being uncorrelated is a precondition for the reporting interaction to begin, nor does it rule out other triggers or conditions.

content: The C2 JU determines that a locally derived ballistic missile track is uncorrelated with ballistic missile tracks reported on the Surveillance NPG.
rationale: The evidence states that the C2 JU must continuously correlate tracks and report uncorrelated ones, but it does not support the specific claim that the trigger is the determination of a track being uncorrelated, nor does it explicitly state this determination as the initiating event for the use case.

content: C2 JU determines whether the data points being detected by its local sensors are currently reported on the interface.
rationale: The evidence explicitly states that each C2 JU has the responsibility to determine whether data points detected by local sensors are currently reported on the interface.

content: C2 JU continuously correlates locally derived ballistic missile tracks with ballistic missile tracks reported on the Surveillance NPG.
rationale: The evidence explicitly states that each C2 JU must continuously correlate locally derived ballistic missile tracks with those reported on the Surveillance NPG.

content: C2 JU reports on all uncorrelated local ballistic missile tracks and assumes R2 for those tracks in accordance with the R2 rules as specified in paragraph 4.4.6.15.
rationale: The claim is directly supported by the parsed source text which states that each C2 JU shall report on all uncorrelated local ballistic missile tracks and assume R2 for those tracks in accordance with specified rules.

content: C2 JU transmits J3.XC1 at next opportunity for new tracks when assuming R2 or when data changes.
rationale: The evidence table states that J3.XC1 is transmitted at the next opportunity for new tracks when assuming R2 or when data changes, but it does not specify that the transmitter is a 'C2 JU' (it specifies 'JU' generally), making the specific actor attribution unsupported.

content: C2 JU reports positional data for ballistic missile tracks in the Space Track message as X, Y, Z position in earth-centered, earth-fixed (ECF) Cartesian coordinates defined by the World Geodetic System-84 (WGS-84) Reference Frame.
rationale: The evidence explicitly states that positional data for ballistic missile tracks are reported in the Space Track message as X, Y, Z position in ECF Cartesian coordinates defined by WGS-84, which directly supports the claim.

content: C2 JU reports the velocity of ballistic missile tracks as the rate of change along the X, Y, Z axis.
rationale: The claim is directly supported by Evidence [milstd6016b_sec4:P68#C216] section 4.4.6.8, which states that the velocity of ballistic missile tracks shall be reported as the rate of change along the X, Y, Z axis.

content: A JU with R2 of a ballistic missile track maintains R2 on the related Impact Point.
rationale: The claim is a direct paraphrase of evidence unit [milstd6016b_sec4:P65#C206] item f, which explicitly states that a JU with R2 of a ballistic missile track shall maintain R2 on the related Impact Point.

content: C2 JU uses the J3.0 Reference Point message to report the actual or expected Launch Point of a ballistic missile; the time of the launch is reported to the nearest second with the Time Function field set to value 4, Departure Time.
rationale: The claim is directly supported by Evidence [milstd6016b_sec4:P65#C207], which explicitly states that the J3.0 Reference Point message is used to report the launch point and specifies the time reporting format.

content: At main flow step 1, if there are conflicts between locally derived information and information reported on the interface, C2 JU shall resolve the difference by transmitting the appropriate J7 message, by operator procedure, or by voice coordination.
rationale: The evidence supports the conflict resolution method but does not support the specific claim that this occurs 'At main flow step 1' or is triggered specifically by that step, as the source describes a continuous correlation responsibility rather than a step-specific alternative flow.

content: At main flow step 3, if a C2 JU with R2 for the Reference TN receives a J7.1 message with the Data Update Request Action field set to value 2, Ballistic Missile Update Request, on a specific TN, the JU shall respond with a J3.6 Space Track message and transmit the data held in the appropriate J3.6 word sequence.
rationale: The evidence explicitly states that a C2 JU with R2 shall respond with a J3.6 Space Track message upon receiving a J7.1 message with Action field set to 2 (Ballistic Missile Update Request), directly supporting all material propositions in the claim.

content: During execution of a DUR response, if an R2 shift occurs where the Number/Frequency of Updates field is set to value 2 or 3, the JU assuming R2 shall not respond to any prior Data Update Request.
rationale: The claim is a direct paraphrase of the final sentence in Evidence [milstd6016b_sec4:P110#C371], which explicitly states the behavior of the JU assuming R2 during an R2 shift with specific field values.

content: At main flow step 6, after predicted impact, there is no requirement to continue transmitting a missile impact point.
rationale: The evidence explicitly states that there is no requirement to continue transmitting a missile impact point after predicted impact, which directly supports the claim.

content: If the predicted time to impact is less than 16 seconds, the JU shall not transmit an initial surveillance report on a ballistic missile; if the altitude of the descending ballistic missile is less than 8 data miles, an initial Ballistic Missile surveillance report shall not be transmitted. Impact points are not subject to this constraint. Exit: do not transmit the initial report.
rationale: The claim's conditions and prohibitions regarding transmission based on time to impact and altitude are directly supported by the parsed source text.

content: If there are conflicts between locally derived information and information reported on the interface, the C2 JU shall resolve the difference by transmitting the appropriate J7 message, by operator procedure, or by voice coordination. Exit: conflict resolved by one of these means.
rationale: The evidence explicitly states that in the event of a conflict between locally derived and interface-reported information, the C2 JU shall resolve the difference via J7 message, operator procedure, or voice coordination.

content: If differences in ballistic missile position or velocity are recognized by a JU, those differences are not resolved through conflict processing and shall not generate a J7.0 message with the Track Management Action field set to value 1, Difference Report; refer to Resolution of Duplicate Track Number, paragraph 4.1.3.7. Exit: do not use conflict processing or generate a Difference Report.
rationale: The claim is directly supported by Evidence [milstd6016b_sec4:P82#C279], which states that differences in ballistic missile position or velocity recognized by a JU are not resolved through conflict processing and shall not generate a J7.0 message with the Track Management Action field set to value 1.

content: If a non-R2 JU receives a J7.1 message with the Data Update Request Action field set to value 2, Ballistic Missile Update Request, on a specific TN, the JU shall not respond. Exit: no response to the J7.1 (ACT = 2) request.
rationale: The evidence explicitly states that Non-R2 JUs shall not respond to a J7.1 (ACT = 2) Ballistic Missile Update Request, which directly supports the claim's condition and outcome.

content: If an R2 shift occurs during execution of a DUR response where the Number/Frequency of Updates field is set to value 2 or 3, the JU assuming R2 shall not respond to any prior Data Update Request. Exit: do not respond to any prior Data Update Request.
rationale: The claim is directly supported by the final sentence of the cited evidence, which explicitly states that if an R2 shift occurs during a DUR response with specific field values, the JU shall not respond to prior requests.

content: There is no requirement to continue transmitting a missile impact point after predicted impact. Exit: no requirement to continue transmitting a missile impact point after predicted impact.
rationale: The evidence explicitly states that there is no requirement to continue transmitting a missile impact point after predicted impact, which directly supports the claim.

content: The C2 JU reports on all uncorrelated local ballistic missile tracks and assumes R2 for those tracks in accordance with the R2 rules specified in paragraph 4.4.6.15.
rationale: The claim is directly supported by the evidence text which states that each C2 JU shall report on all uncorrelated local ballistic missile tracks and assume R2 for those tracks.

content: The positional data for ballistic missile tracks are reported in the Space Track message as X, Y, Z position in earth-centered, earth-fixed (ECF) Cartesian coordinates defined by the World Geodetic System-84 (WGS-84) Reference Frame.
rationale: The claim is a direct paraphrase of the evidence in section 4.4.6.7, which explicitly states that ballistic missile positional data are reported in Space Track messages as X, Y, Z ECF Cartesian coordinates defined by WGS-84.

content: The velocity of ballistic missile tracks is reported as the rate of change along the X, Y, Z axis.
rationale: The claim is directly supported by Evidence [milstd6016b_sec4:P68#C216] section 4.4.6.8, which states that the velocity of ballistic missile tracks shall be reported as the rate of change along the X, Y, Z axis.

content: The J3.0 Reference Point message is used to report the actual or expected Launch Point of a ballistic missile; the time of the launch is reported to the nearest second with the Time Function field set to value 4, Departure Time.
rationale: The claim is a direct paraphrase of the evidence text in section 4.4.6.3(a), which explicitly states the purpose of the J3.0 Reference Point message and the specific time reporting format.

content: If a conflict existed between locally derived information and information reported on the interface, the C2 JU has resolved the difference by transmitting the appropriate J7 message, by operator procedure, or by voice coordination.
rationale: The claim is directly supported by Evidence [milstd6016b_sec4:P68#C216], which states that in the event of conflict, the C2 JU shall resolve the difference by transmitting the appropriate J7 message, by operator procedure, or by voice coordination.

content: To exchange surveillance information on the Link 16 network by transmitting ballistic missile track/point data that is as complete, accurate, and timely as possible.
